facts.statement: Xianshanosaurus was described in 2009 by a team of paleontologists led by Lü Junchang.
facts.quote: It was described in 2009 by a team of paleontologists led by Lü Junchang.

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae of Xianshanosaurus were procoelous, meaning they had concave front faces and convex back faces that formed ball-and-socket joints, a trait typical of titanosaurs.
facts.quote: The caudal vertebrae are procoelous, a feature characteristic of titanosaurs, in which the vertebrae have strongly concave anterior faces and strongly convex posterior faces forming ball-and-socket articulations between the vertebrae.

facts.statement: Unlike many titanosaurs, the back ribs of Xianshanosaurus lacked pneumatic openings and the haemal arches had closed canals.
facts.quote: Unlike titanosaurs, the dorsal ribs do not have pneumatic openings and the haemal arches have a closed canal.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Xianshanosaurus is a titanosaur, and its closest relative may be Daxiatitan, though its evolutionary relationships remain controversial.
facts.quote: Xianshanosaurus may be a titanosaur, and Daxiatitan may be its closest relative, but its evolutionary relationships remain controversial.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses have often regarded Xianshanosaurus as an unstable taxon with uncertain placement.
facts.quote: Studies that have included Xianshanosaurus in phylogenetic analyses have regarded it as an unstable taxon.

facts.statement: In some analyses where Euhelopodidae was treated as a non-neosauropod group, researchers recovered Daxiatitan as the sister taxon to Xianshanosaurus.
facts.quote: In the third case, in which Euhelopodidae was recovered as a non-neosauropod clade equivalent to Mamenchisauridae, Moore et al. recovered Daxiatitan as the sister taxon of Xianshanosaurus.

facts.statement: Xianshanosaurus lived in the middle of the Cretaceous period, approximately between 125 and 100 million years ago, from the Aptian to Albian stages in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 125 a 100 millones de años, desde el Aptiense al Albiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Xianshanosaurus were found in the Mangchuan Formation in the Ruyang Basin, specifically in Shijiagou village, Liudian town, Luoyang city, Henan province, China.
facts.quote: Fue encontrado en la Formación Mangchuan, en el bajio Ruyang, villa Shijiagou, pueblo Liudian de la ciudad Luoyang, provincia de Henan, China.

facts.statement: The time range for Xianshanosaurus is estimated from 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago, spanning the Aptian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Xianshanosaurus as Euhelopodidae.
